Pulse for 27 October 2026

The stories from 27 October 2026 in the Pulse of the Sapaude app, in our own words. Terms you don’t know are explained in the glossary. Glossary

Everyday tool

ChatGPT reads iCloud mail

A plugin is an add-on that lets ChatGPT reach another service, and on 27 October 2026 OpenAI made iCloud Mail and iCloud Calendar plugins available on every ChatGPT plan on the web, the desktop app, and iOS.

New model

Steer a world the AI builds

A world model is a program that generates a place you can move through, and Google DeepMind says Genie 4, its new one, lets you steer that place with a keyboard and with text while the sound is generated with the picture.

AI agents

AI drafts, labs still test

A drug candidate is a molecule a lab hopes might become a medicine, and Anthropic wrote on 27 October 2026 that partners used Claude on designs and on long documents that are still at an early, mostly preclinical stage.

Everyday tool

Copilot learns from mail

Memory, here, is a store of details an assistant keeps so the next answer needs less setup, and Forbes reported on 27 October 2026 that Microsoft 365 Copilot now also draws inferences from your work mail, chats, and meeting notes.

New model

Edit a photo by asking

An image edit is a change to a picture you already have, and Microsoft says its new model, MAI Image 2.7, makes that change from a written instruction and launches in preview.

AI agents

Experts adopt AI's choices

An agent is a program that can use tools and argue for one option, and Anthropic reported on 27 October 2026 that 50 professional analysts matched that program's hidden lean on 86 percent of the analytical choices in its study.

Everyday tool

Slides and docs get AI help

An assistant is a helper built into the app you already use for a deck or a memo, and Apple says the November update adds one to Pages, Keynote, and Numbers that can work from the file you have open.

New model

Small models run on laptops

A small model is a compact AI program whose numbers can sit on a laptop, and Liquid AI says its new LFM3 family does that for text, pictures, and sound, including runs that need no cloud connection.
